- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

# Event subscriptions

Last updated Oct 15, 2026|Copy as Markdown| [View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/event-subscriptions/index.md)| [Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/)

[Event subscriptions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/event-subscriptions/) allow you to receive messages when events occur across your Cloudflare account. Cloudflare products (e.g., [KV](https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/), [Workers AI](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/), [Workers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/)) can publish structured events to a [queue](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/), which you can then consume with Workers or [HTTP pull consumers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/pull-consumers/) to build custom workflows, integrations, or logic.

For more information on [Event Subscriptions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/event-subscriptions/), refer to the [management guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/event-subscriptions/manage-event-subscriptions/).

## Available Email Sending events

Email Sending event subscriptions publish outbound transactional email lifecycle events for messages sent from an enabled sending domain. Each subscription is scoped to one sending domain: either the zone apex, such as `example.com`, or a verified sending subdomain, such as `send.example.com`.

Email Routing events, including inbound forwards, replies, Worker-emitted routing events, and deliveries to verified routing recipients, are not published as Email Sending events.

#### `message.delivered`

Triggered when the recipient mail server accepts the message.

**Example:**

```json

	"type": "cf.email.sending.message.delivered",
	"source": {
		"type": "email.sending",
		"zoneId": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353",
		"domain": "example.com"
	},
	"payload": {
		"eventId": "0190d0c4-7e9a-7b3c-9f12-1a2b3c4d5e6f",

		"sender": "noreply@example.com",
		"recipient": "user@example.net",
		"subject": "Welcome",
		"terminal": true,
		"delivery": {

			"deliveryTimeMs": 1234,

			"smtpResponse": "250 2.0.0 OK 1714820445 a1b2c3 - gsmtp"
		}
	},

	}
}
```

Executor is a host that runs apps: TypeScript packages that expose tools,
storage, UI, accounts and background work. Agents reach every app through the
MCP tools `skills`, `search`, `describe`, `call` and `execute`, with each app's
slug as its namespace. Credentials go only through Executor's secure connection
links, never through chat or source code. Some calls pause for user approval.

`tools.<slug>.<tool>`, and input type; `describe({ paths })` returns full
signatures. Never guess argument names.

in your way, can't do something you need, works especially well, or the user

reporting. Be specific; never include credentials or user data (`feedback.md`).

**(1) Message body shape**

The page does not label these examples as "queue message body," but it says events are published to a queue and each example is a complete event. Each event has four top-level keys: `type`, `source`, `payload`, `metadata`.

- `type`: string, for example `cf.email.sending.message.delivered`
- `source`: `type` (fixed value `email.sending`), `zoneId`, `domain` (the zone apex or the sending subdomain)
- `payload`:
  - `eventId`
  - `messageId`
  - `sender`
  - `recipient`
  - `subject` (absent from the `message.complained` example)
  - `terminal` (boolean)
  - `delivery`: `status`, `provider`, `deliveryTimeMs`, `smtpStatusCode`, `smtpEnhancedStatusCode`, `smtpResponse`. In the `message.failed` and `message.rejected` examples, `delivery` contains only `status`.
  - `bounce` (deferred and bounced only): `type`, `classification`, `reason`
  - `failure` (failed only): `reason`
  - `rejection` (rejected only): `reason`, `party`, `detail`
  - `complaint` (complained only): `type`
- `metadata`: `accountId`, `eventSubscriptionId`, `eventSchemaVersion` (example value `1`), `eventTimestamp`

Documented value examples:
- `bounce.type`: `"soft"` (deferred), `"hard"` (bounced)
- `bounce.classification`: `"temporary_failure"` (deferred), `"permanent_failure"` (bounced)
- `delivery.status`: `"delivered"`, `"deferred"`, `"bounced"`, `"failed"`, `"rejected"`, `"complained"`
- `delivery.provider`: `"gmail"`, `"external_smtp"`
- `failure.reason`: `"delivery_failed"`
- `rejection.reason`: `"suppressed"`; `rejection.party`: `"recipient"`
- `complaint.type`: `"abuse"`
- `metadata.eventTimestamp` example: `"2026-06-01T02:48:57.132Z"`

Timestamps: the only timestamp field is `metadata.eventTimestamp`. `delivery.deliveryTimeMs` is a number (example `1234`), not a timestamp.

SMTP fields: `delivery.smtpStatusCode` (string, e.g. `"250"`, `"451"`, `"550"`), `delivery.smtpEnhancedStatusCode` (string, e.g. `"5.1.1"`), `delivery.smtpResponse` (string, e.g. `"550 5.1.1 User unknown"`).

**(2) Event type strings**

The `type` field values are:
- `cf.email.sending.message.delivered` (recipient server accepted the message)
- `cf.email.sending.message.deferred` (temporary failure, retries pending)
- `cf.email.sending.message.bounced` (permanent bounce, or temporary retries exhausted)
- `cf.email.sending.message.failed` (internal or non-SMTP delivery error)
- `cf.email.sending.message.rejected` (rejected before delivery by policy: suppression, validation, or spam)
- `cf.email.sending.message.complained` (recipient marked a delivered message as spam via feedback loop)

The page's section headings use the shorter forms `message.delivered`, `message.deferred`, `message.bounced`, `message.failed`, `message.rejected`, `message.complained`.
